title: openai-compat: support Responses variants, deterministic-seed flag, and metadata passthrough
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Several downstream partners expect a closer match to the OpenAI Responses surface, including variant response shapes, a deterministic seed/determinism flag, and request-level metadata passthrough that should round-trip into the returned response objects. This PR implements a compatibility layer and a guarded rollout that maps Redwood internal request fields to OpenAI-style Responses semantics while preserving our runtime invariants. High-level changes: 1) Responses variants: added an adapter that exposes the /v1/responses-like shapes (items, outputs, content blocks) and translates our streaming deltas into SSE-compatible delta chunks. The adapter supports both simple text responses and structured output blocks used by tool-calling. 2) Deterministic seed flag: introduced an optional query/body flag deterministic_seed and seed that signals repeatable sampling; this is translated into our sampling backend in a best-effort way (we document cases where exact determinism cannot be guaranteed, e.g., mixed-precision quantized kernels across GPUs). 3) Metadata passthrough: request.metadata is now propagated to response.metadata and preserved across retries and fallback model routing; audit logging records the original metadata for traceability. 4) Streaming stability improvements: hardened the chunk encoder, added rate-aware buffering to avoid partial JSON frames for structured outputs, and introduced backpressure knobs to reduce client-visible reorder under heavy batching. Implementation notes: - New package go/openai/compat/responses_adapter.go implements mapping logic and exposes a thin shim used by the OpenAI-compat HTTP handler. - Python and TypeScript SDK adapters updated to accept the new deterministic_seed/seed parameters and to surface response.metadata in typed objects. Files changed include unit and integration tests that validate deterministic runs across fixed RNG seeds and a compatibility test that replays a set of recorded OpenAI Responses fixtures. Rollout plan: feature is behind a feature-flag openai_responses_compat; start with internal customers set to opt-in, run A/B traffic for 48h, then enable by default if no regressions. Backwards compatibility: legacy OpenAI-compat endpoints continue to function; when deterministic_seed is absent we keep prior sampling behavior. Known limitations: exact bitwise reproducibility is not guaranteed across heterogeneous hardware; structured-tool step boundaries rely on the consumer respecting output markers. Checklist: implement adapter, wire SDK surfaces, add unit/integration tests, add docs snippet for determinism and metadata, gated rollout, monitor regressions.

release_notes: - OpenAI Responses compatibility adapter: supports Responses variants and SSE delta mapping. - New deterministic_seed + seed parameters for best-effort repeatable sampling. - Request metadata is preserved and surfaced on response.metadata for OpenAI-compat requests. See docs/openai-responses-compat.md for caveats and rollout plan.
